<objective>
Create the two SHARED presentational sub-components (D-01, D-02) that both modals will embed: `MeasurementRulerComponent` (ruler SVG + draggable endpoints + preset buttons) and `AttachmentPointPickerComponent` (crosshair click-to-place overlay + point marker + define/cancel toggle). Both are UI-only shells over the Plan 02 services — they own their template and `.scss`, take current state via decorator `@Input()`, and emit plain value objects via decorator `@Output()`. They never import `@angular/forms` or write to a parent form (D-01 form-agnostic contract; RESEARCH.md Pitfall 1).

Reference structure: `category-dropdown.component.ts` (standalone, own template + scss) — but DO NOT copy its `input()`/`output()` signal syntax; D-02 locks THIS phase to `@Input()`/`@Output()` decorators to match the existing modal style.

Ruler asymmetry to handle (discovered in template review): the edit-modal ruler additionally renders a directional arrow, inline chevrons, and a flip-direction control (edit-modal HTML lines 62-88, methods getRulerArrowPoints/getRulerArrowTransform/getInlineChevronTransforms/getChevronPoints/flipMeasurementDirection at edit-modal lines 520-598). upload-modal's ruler has none of these. The shared component renders the base ruler always and this directional decoration only when an `@Input() showDirection` flag is true — so one component serves both without duplicating the SVG.

This plan creates the components; wiring them into the modal shells is Plans 06/07 (Wave 4).
Output: two new component directories (ts/html/scss/spec each).
</objective>

Declare decorator inputs `@Input({ required: true }) imageElement!: HTMLImageElement | null;`, `@Input() line: MeasurementLine | null = null;`, `@Input() showDirection = false;`, and output `@Output() lineChange = new EventEmitter<MeasurementLine>();` (plus `@Output() flip = new EventEmitter<void>()` if flip is surfaced) — decorator style per D-02, NOT `input()`/`output()`.
